note: Risk register (founder decision company/decisions/2026-10-14-founder-risk-in-ops-review.md). Owner: principal-engineer-ops. Format: company/ops/risks.md. Re-scored at every Operational Health Review (company/rituals/templates/ops-review.md, section 7). Check: node tools/risks.mjs report.

risks.title: Single 4-CPU shared host
risks.description: Every agent, build, dev server, QA run and git worktree shares one 4-CPU box. On 10-14 it ran at load 25-60 with disk full several times (ENOSPC, git could not write refs); QA could not run until load fell to ~5 at 18:00. One `next dev` on :3530 serves every agent, so one fault takes all of them down. No role owns the host (principal-engineer holds it interim). 2026-10-15 (W-923): First Light pre-mortem row 5 (two migrations on one 4-CPU host, L3 I3) and the host half of proposed FL-01 are carried here. The early-warning signal is load over 8 or free disk under 15 GB on a First Light build day (`node tools/ops-health.mjs`).

mitigation.summary: Host allocator: dispatch-check C1/C2/C4 refuses over 8 agents / 3 builders, load > 2x CPUs or < 10 GB free (built 18:25, caps await ratification W-712, run before every dispatch W-713); interim 2 concurrent builds/QA (W-532); disk prune and pre-build guard (W-525); capacity decision, second machine or runner (W-531); a named owner (W-533).
mitigation.paperOnly: W-525 guard and prune are not built; W-531 has no record; W-533 has no owner; the 8/3 caps are proposed, not ratified, and dispatch-check is a step someone must remember to run.

risks.title: CI cost per push: the queue never drains
risks.description: Every push queues a full `ci` (npm ci, build, Playwright, full QA), about 1 runner-hour each. At 19:06 on 10-14, 278 runs were queued, the oldest 9 h old; `ci` has not gone green for a current commit, so `deploy.yml` never fires. The one-off drain (W-774) is blocked: the session token has no `actions: write` (HTTP 403 on all 277 cancels). AMD-002 stops new duplicates on a ref but cannot reach the backlog or cut the per-push cost.

mitigation.summary: Containment AMD-002 (in place). Root fix: per-push cost cut (changed-lesson QA, sharding, timeouts) via AMD-007 (W-775). Drain once (W-774, needs a token with actions: write or the founder to cancel). Meter (W-776) and back-pressure on pushers (W-777). Falsifier 10-16 (W-481).
mitigation.paperOnly: Only AMD-002 exists. W-775 needs an amendment not yet drafted; W-776/W-777 are backlog; W-774 is blocked on a permission.

risks.title: Production deploys bypass CI (W-480)
risks.description: Vercel's git integration builds `[deploy]` commits on its own trigger and never waits for `ci`. All four 10-14 deploys shipped before CI judged them (G1), so `constitution` and `verify` are advisory for anything that reaches learners, including an unratified protected-path change. The guard (`[deploy]` string filter in `vercel.json`) is unprotected and was edited by a `[deploy]` commit (J3). Anyone who can type `[deploy]` can ship. 2026-10-15 (W-923): First Light pre-mortem row 4 (launched through a path with no gate, L3 I4) is carried here, and W-480 is a First Light go/no-go item. Drafts half: it does not move until r7's C2 checks pass on the production domain (readiness record 2026-10-15-r7-drafts-trust-sheet.md, C2). r7 has not shipped (the last entry in releases.json is r6), so the entry stays open at L4 I5 and the drafts half is unchanged. When C2 passes, the drafts half may go to in-place for page reachability only. Drafts' meta and code stay in the client chunk (W-946), and the deploy-bypass half is unchanged.

mitigation.summary: Root fix: production only via `deploy.yml` after green `ci` (Vercel git production builds off, or a Deployment Check on `ci`), drafts unreachable, decision record with the founder (W-480). Containment: founder approval per deploy and the `[deploy]` filter (cost controls, not gates). Snapshots refuse protected paths and record `check` (W-482).
mitigation.paperOnly: The fix (W-480) is not started. What exists is a CLAUDE.md rule and a filter in an unprotected file; neither is a gate. Note R-002: even after W-480, deploys wait on a CI that does not conclude.

risks.title: /spike S1 still open on production until a deploy
risks.description: `/spike?cdn=` let anyone frame any site under our domain and write learners' localStorage and `/api/events`. The code fix (W-477) is done and in review, but production still runs the old build, and nothing ships without a founder-approved deploy. The fix only reaches learners through the path R-003 describes.

mitigation.summary: Fixed in code (W-477, done). Ship it: founder-approved deploy (W-584) with the post-deploy smoke that checks `/spike` and `/spike?cdn=` return 404 (W-609); the release hold (W-534) lifts once W-477's review passes.
mitigation.paperOnly: The fix is real but not live; exposure on production is unchanged until the deploy.

risks.title: In-review lessons shown in production (W-479 G2)
risks.description: Production shows lessons that have not passed the publish gates behind an "In review" tag (238+ cited by the constitutional review; 271 lessons are in `review` on disk now, carrying most of the 193 unverified claims). No override decision record exists under Article 4.1, and `review` status is a hand edit (G3). Latent: with `SHOW_REVIEW` unset, `findDemo()` serves any `draft` (66 drafts on disk now) by direct URL after the next deploy.

mitigation.summary: Founder: write the override with an exit date, or set `SHOW_REVIEW=off` in production (W-479 item 4). Drafts never reachable in production (W-480). Ops review declares SEV1 if undecided at the next review.
mitigation.paperOnly: Only the "In review" tag exists. No decision, no exit date, no draft block.

risks.title: Held claims on sources this host cannot open
risks.description: Fact-checkers hold claims they cannot verify because the host's proxy blocks gov, health, pubmed and arxiv sources (6-10 held per FC batch). On disk now: 193 unverified claims across 100 lessons, and 107 lessons whose claim records mention an unopened or unopenable source. (The brief's "about 295 lessons" was not reproducible from meta.json; my count is above, method: claims with status != verified, and claim text matching held/unopen.) The stage-only reword precedent (J5) keeps learners from false facts but moves lessons towards describing only themselves, and nobody tracks the total. 2026-10-15 (W-923): behavioral-econ pre-mortem row 2 is carried here (L4 I3). Every replication verdict in its case is the author's prior from memory, the expected held-claim rate is 30-40%, and the signal is a pilot held-claim rate over 25% at the first fact-check, or the sourcing note (W-902) missing when the pilot is briefed.

mitigation.summary: One web-capable fact-check session per wave (founder, W-583). A single stage-only reword log with restore items (W-483). Re-check queues by host (W-385, W-511, W-490).
mitigation.paperOnly: No egress decision, no reword log; held claims accumulate.

risks.title: Books copyright, and no legal read
risks.description: Book Summaries paraphrase copyrighted books. The charter says no Books lesson publishes before the founder rules on a legal read, but that is a charter rule: no publish hold or gate checks it, and Books drafts and pilot builds already exist.

mitigation.summary: Founder: commission the legal read and name a book source (W-541, W-615 F1/F2). Proposed: a publish hold for every books-domain slug until the ruling (chief-of-staff, publish-holds.json).
mitigation.paperOnly: The only control is a sentence in the charter. Nothing mechanical stops a Books publish.

risks.title: Sensitive-topics route not active (W-626)
risks.description: History, Big Ideas and Books briefs include sensitive classes (slavery, war, political figures). The cultural-reviewer route that should review them before publish is a proposed patch, and the gate (AMD-006) is not drafted. History briefs 3, 4, 5 and 11 already need it (W-744).

mitigation.summary: Founder decides the cultural-reviewer patch (W-764); localization-lead consents to the load (W-765); AMD-006 publish gate (W-766); CMs mark sensitive briefs (W-767, W-768, W-769).
mitigation.paperOnly: No route, no gate, no marked briefs.

risks.title: Board-ID collisions (W-528)
risks.description: `board add` allocates `max + 1` of the local file (protected `tools/company.mjs`). Parallel sessions and stale worktree branches collide; on 10-14 ids were renumbered by hand and at least 3 updates were overwritten (audit A4, F9). The loser of a race silently loses an item.

mitigation.summary: Concurrency-safe allocator by amendment, falsifier: 20 parallel adds give 20 ids, 0 lost (W-528). Single-writer rule for board.json (chief of staff only).
mitigation.paperOnly: The amendment is not drafted, and the single-writer rule is contradicted by CLAUDE.md and the role docs (audit F5).

risks.title: Event-log gap (W-716)
risks.description: The event log stopped recording dispatches and reports at about 16:00 on 10-14 while git took about 50 commits (audit F4; WBR logging check). Everything computed from it is blind for that window: rituals-due thresholds, concurrency, stop rate, metrics, the token ledger (about 64 runs missing).

mitigation.summary: Find why the hooks stopped, fix, backfill (W-716). rituals-due already counts committed ritual records as held (workaround in place).
mitigation.paperOnly: The cause is not found; the records workaround covers rituals only, not dispatch, usage or concurrency.

risks.title: No real-learner data
risks.description: `/api/events` only `console.log`s, there is no auth or progress database (F-01), and no real learner has used a lesson (EXP-002 not started). Every learning claim the company makes is simulated. Even a deploy produces no data until events persist.

mitigation.summary: Persist events (W-706, after the founder's F-01 auth/DB decision); deploy (W-584); recruit 5 learners (W-007, F-11).
mitigation.paperOnly: Nothing persists; no provider chosen; no learner recruited.

risks.title: Usage budget: unmeasured unit, no approved budgets
risks.description: The 10-13 usage limit stopped 8 of 9 builders mid-wave. The 20x upgrade removed the stops (2 of 346 on 10-14), but no project has an approved budget, 82% of spend is attributed by role default, the coordinator's spend and 32 stopped runs are unmeasured, and nobody knows whether `subagent_tokens` is the billed unit. A budget that is not in the billed unit cannot warn before the limit. 2026-10-15 (W-923): First Light pre-mortem row 2 is carried here (L4 I3). No backend-engineer, learner-model-engineer, personalization-lead, growth-designer or privacy-reviewer run exists in the ledger, so every unit is a proxy. Signal: `ledger.mjs report --project=first-light` past 2.9M before W-908. Behavioral-econ pre-mortem row 4 is also carried here (L4 I2): measured category set-up of about 1.2M against the 0.1M assumed. Signal: `--project=behavioral-econ` past 1.46M before the DLR five are reviewed.

mitigation.summary: Ledger and `ledger.mjs gate` (built; grace to 10-16); project rule in dispatch-check (W-720); `[project:<id>]` tags (W-721); token unit (W-728, principal-engineer-ops); first Project Review sets budgets (F-15).
mitigation.paperOnly: The ledger exists; the gate is not wired into dispatch, no budget is set, and the unit is unknown.

risks.title: Founder bandwidth
risks.description: The founder is on the critical path of most red items: 20 open board items and 13 open founder-inbox items, including the deploy path (W-480), in-review lessons (W-479), the first deploy (W-584), web fact-checks (W-583), Books legal (W-541), auth/DB (F-01), operating caps (W-712), the sensitive route (W-764), capacity spend (W-531) and Project Review 1 (F-15). Founder asks also turned into dispatch with no capacity answer (audit F2). 2026-10-15 (W-923): First Light pre-mortem row 1 is carried here (founder decisions on the path, L4 I4, confirmed in the 10-15 re-score). The path holds four founder decisions in 15 days: F-15 (10-16), F-01 (10-23, open since 10-13), F-19 (10-30) and the freeze acceptance. If F-01 is still open on 10-23, head-of-strategic-initiatives proposes impact 5 for that row. The entry's own score (L5 I4) is unchanged until the ops review.

mitigation.summary: Founder-request intake rule and daily rhythm (audit sections 2-3, ratify W-712); one ranked founder inbox with a recommendation per item; founder digest twice a day; delegate what the constitution allows (Project Review delegation, F-15 item 0).
mitigation.paperOnly: The inbox and digest exist; the intake rule and delegation are proposals; nothing ranks the founder queue by risk.

risks.title: COE actions do not close
risks.description: The 10-13 COE's five actions have no board ids (ops review action 15, still owed). The three 10-14 COEs are final, but almost all their actions are backlog, one is blocked (W-774), and the root-cause fixes need amendments (W-775, W-528) or founder decisions (W-480, W-531). A COE whose actions stall repeats.

mitigation.summary: dispatch-check R2: no build waves while a SEV1/SEV2 lacks a final COE (built, review W-715). Each ops review lists slipped COE actions (template section 7). Chief of staff gives the 10-13 actions board ids or drops them.
mitigation.paperOnly: R2 checks that a COE exists, not that its actions close.

risks.title: Protected-path check leaks (G5) and gates in ordinary tooling (G6)
risks.description: CI's constitution job diffs from `event.before`, skips the first push of a new branch, and accepts any ratified AMD for any protected path; the hook has the same flaw. AMD-001 is still proposed, so gate logic lives in unprotected tools (publish-ready.mjs), easier to change than what it judges.

mitigation.summary: Founder commissions AMD-003 (fixed base, no skip, per-AMD path lists) and decides AMD-001 (W-479).
mitigation.paperOnly: Not drafted; the board has not asked.

risks.title: Red `check` is routine
risks.description: Half-built domains on the shared tree turn `npm run check` red for everyone; "check fails, not mine" became normal and hides real errors (G4). WIP snapshots push with check failing.

mitigation.summary: Decide how WIP domains stop failing check (W-530); snapshots record check status (W-482).
mitigation.paperOnly: Neither built.

risks.title: Agent isolation: wrong worktree, process kills, scratch collisions
risks.description: Agents wrote into the coordinator's worktree, `pkill -f` patterns killed the coordinator's shell twice (a repeat of closed W-072), background loops died with their parent, and scratch dirs collided. Each is a SEV3 today; the promotion rule makes the next lost commit a SEV2. 2026-10-15: builders' dev and QA ports cross-talked (hist-1's :3621 served hist-3's slugs), so QA and walkthroughs judged a neighbour's build (W-851). This is a failure mode of this entry, not a separate risk.

mitigation.summary: Worktree-per-agent lifecycle (W-526), pid-file process wrapper and no pattern kills (W-529), per-agent scratch dirs (W-023). Port cross-talk (W-851): tools refuse a taken port (tools-batch a368240, merged), and QA no longer reuses a server it did not start unless QA_REUSE_SERVER=1 (3b97991, approved with conditions 2026-10-15).
mitigation.paperOnly: dispatch-check C3 exists; the lifecycle script, wrapper and scratch dirs do not.

risks.title: Volume counted instead of Surface Value
risks.description: The plan to 2,000 can be met by counting files: Life Hacks has 200 lessons and 0 publishable, and 45% of lessons needed rework. Building faster than review raises the queue, not the count, and puts pressure on evaluator independence (plan-to-2000 section 6).

mitigation.summary: Count only published lessons towards 2,000; wave gate (no Wave K builder claims until the review queue is at most one wave and J is at least 60% published; W-556, decided); walkthrough before account, always (evaluation-steward).
mitigation.paperOnly: The wave gate is a decision checked by the chief of staff, not by a tool.

risks.title: Shared lesson engines fail many lessons at once
risks.description: Life Hacks runs 200 lessons on four engines (Home, Study, Resource, AlphabetSearch). In r9 batch D, 14 of 14 lessons needed revision, and the WBR hypothesis (a) is one engine bug (inverted mode toggle, no amounts row) failing them all the same way. An engine change has the blast radius of a kit change but is reviewed like a lesson.

mitigation.summary: Engines v2 (W-608, in review by accessibility-reviewer and the spec); readiness check at change tier 2 for any engine or template used by more than 10 lessons (company/rituals/templates/ops-readiness.md).
mitigation.paperOnly: v2 is in review, not merged; the readiness check is proposed (EDD-007) and not enforced by a tool yet.

risks.title: Review capacity for tier-2 readiness and privacy is First Light's critical path
risks.description: Proposed as FL-06 (risk-rescore.md, 2026-10-15). This is the tech lead's objection 5 to the head-of-strategic-initiatives role, extended by the evaluation steward (quality-bar.md section 3). Auth, server-side progress, the database, the event API and the deploy are tier 2 (EDD-007), and each needs EDD, then PE review, then privacy data-model review (D-17), then readiness approval, in series, before its first code run. A rework round restarts the chain (dependencies.md section 2). Measured: privacy-reviewer has never run and First Light asks it for about 13 runs, plus the gate criteria by 10-22 (W-932) and the rulings by 11-09. principal-engineer-ops has 3 measured runs before 10-15 (81k mean). The one prior tier-2 approval (r7) took two rounds in one day. W-978 was committed at 10:07 UTC and approved at about 10:12 on 10-15. The quality team's ~64 runs are unbudgeted (W-929). Impact is 5, not 4. A launch slip on auth alone would be a 4. But the way this risk fails under pressure is a thin or skipped privacy or readiness review, which ships learner data unreviewed (the scale's 'data exposed'). Conflict noted: the owner is also the register's writer and one of the two constrained reviewers. The score may not be lowered without principal-engineer at an ops review.

mitigation.summary: Budget the review lines in the tranche-1 approval (privacy-reviewer, principal-engineer-ops, PE reviews, the W-929 quality line) and give First Light reviews priority in the weeks of 10-19, 11-09 and 11-16 (portfolio-manager). Queue the auth EDD, privacy data-model review (D-17) and readiness records as board items before code (chief of staff). principal-engineer-ops reports each First Light readiness record's approval time at the Friday review. If the median passes 4 h for a week, use EDD-007's fallback and delegate one team's tier-2 approvals to principal-engineer. Privacy gate criteria by 10-22 (W-932). The cut order is in the stop rule (head-of-product decides).
mitigation.paperOnly: Mitigations 1 and 2 have no board item: the review lines are not named in any approval, and D-17, the auth EDD and the readiness records are not on the board. Approval time is not measured by a tool (readiness.mjs, EDD-007, does not exist). privacy-reviewer has never run. W-929 and W-932 are backlog.

risks.title: Scale-stage-1 work (the all-metas fix, A1) is pulled onto First Light's critical path
risks.description: Proposed as FL-07, merged with FL-01 (two big migrations at once). Measured (quality-bar.md Q5): first-load JS is 2.32 MB gz against a 500 KB bar (Q5.3), and the feed is usable at 16.7 s against 3.0 s at 4x throttle (Q5.4). W-946 found the 5.3 MB client chunk that carries all 960 metas. The fix (EDD-001 option 4 / EDD-003 A1) needs AMD-001 (c2) (F-03, open since 10-12) and sits in scale-stage-1, which the founder kept off the critical path. If Q5 holds, First Light and stage 1 change the kit and deploy path at the same time, which is FL-01's concern. The host half of FL-01 is in R-001. 2026-10-16 (W-1134, FL-07 re-score proposed L2 I4): the fix is on main. AMD-001's status line reads '(c2)+R1 applied, 0d76ae1', and src/demos/index.generated.ts and loaders.generated.ts are on disk. principal-engineer approved it with changes, and principal-engineer-ops approved readiness with conditions A1 to A6 on 10-16 (2026-10-15-amd001-c2-split.md). What is left: the founder-approved deploy, the steward's audit, and the Q5.3 and Q5.4 re-measure on production (W-607, W-669). Re-scored L4 to L2 by principal-engineer-ops outside an ops review (not the owner's area, and the mechanism is in code). The next ops review confirms or reverts it. Signal for going back to L4: the post-deploy re-measure misses Q5.3 or Q5.4, so more stage-1 work comes onto the path. Accounts and A1 now meet only on the deploy path, which is R-003.

mitigation.summary: principal-engineer answers by 10-22 whether Q5 is reachable and, if so, moves A1 onto the path with its own readiness record (W-930). Emit lesson loaders from a module with no meta imports (W-946, needs an amendment). Stage 1 otherwise runs only as the 50-lesson pilot off the path, and the scale stop rule stops any stage-1 work that blocks a go/no-go item.
mitigation.paperOnly: The split is merged on main but not deployed. Q5.3 and Q5.4 are not re-measured on production. The scale stop rule is a decision-record rule, and no tool checks it.

risks.title: Accounts launch without a privacy, terms and age-gate read
risks.description: Proposed as FL-03 (status.json). It is the same risk as First Light pre-mortem row 3, and the two are merged here. Anonymous-first auth keeps history at sign-up, so learner data exists from day one. Server-side progress, light social and an ad slot go live while the age policy is undecided (F-01, open since 10-13). Under-13 learners bring COPPA and GDPR-K duties. privacy-reviewer has never run, and its data-model review (D-17) has no board item.

mitigation.summary: Privacy-reviewer rulings before tranche-2 social and ad-slot work (the stop rule cuts them by 11-09 otherwise). Privacy gate criteria by 10-22 (W-932). 13+ at launch is the standing recommendation in F-01. Legal workstream. Signal: any table or event holding a learner id merged before a privacy ruling, or an age-gate path missing from the go/no-go readiness list.
mitigation.paperOnly: No privacy-reviewer run exists. D-17 has no board item. F-01 is open. Nothing blocks a merge of a learner-id table without a ruling.

risks.title: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial: accounts or ads on it break the host's terms
risks.description: Proposed as FL-05 (status.json, L4 I3). Production runs on Vercel's free Hobby plan (CLAUDE.md, runbook-deploy.md), which is for non-commercial use. An ad slot, or accounts as part of a commercial product, on Hobby breaks the terms. That puts the production account, and with it every deploy and the feed, at the host's discretion. Impact is raised to 4 from the proposed 3, because losing the production account means the company cannot ship (the scale's 4). The founder's Pro decision (F-18) and W-893/W-908 have not confirmed the requirement yet.

mitigation.summary: Confirm the Pro requirement and price before launch (W-893, W-908). The founder decides the spend (F-18). No ad slot or commercial account flow ships to a Hobby project (go/no-go item).
mitigation.paperOnly: Both items are backlog. Nothing in the deploy path checks the plan.

risks.title: Behavioral economics has too little ground of its own
risks.description: Behavioral-econ pre-mortem row 1. About 30 of the subject's concepts already sit in Economics, Probability, Books and Big Ideas. Only about 15-18 are collision-free, and 5 of the scout's 12 are close calls (2026-10-15-behavioral-economics.md section 3). The famous effects (anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, decoy) stay with Books. head-of-product cut the slot line from 40 to 18 for this reason (W-897, F-22 to the founder).

mitigation.summary: Boundary rulings and the 18-lesson slot line (W-897, done). Neighbour sign-offs before lessons 4 and 5 (playbook step 7). Stop rules: pause if 3 of the DLR five are rejected as duplicates, fold if fewer than 12 collision-free concepts remain after sign-off.
mitigation.paperOnly: The neighbours' written sign-offs (cm-books, cm-economics) are not on disk and have no board id here. F-22 (the slot line) is with the founder.

risks.title: An idle org: a behavioral-econ manager before the pilot passes
risks.description: Behavioral-econ pre-mortem row 3. The category variant adds a category manager before the DLR five have passed. The CEO office named that failure for History. Signal: cm-behavioral created (W-899) before the head-of-product boundary rulings are on disk. Those rulings landed on 10-15 (W-897), so the remaining exposure is strand managers created early.

mitigation.summary: Playbook order: one category manager after step 3, and strand managers only after the DLR five pass (founder decision F-21, step 5). The org-change record is W-899.
mitigation.paperOnly: The order is a decision-record rule, and no tool checks it.

risks.title: Release 1 misses its dates at full scope
risks.description: Proposed as FL-02 (status.json, L4 I4). The 10-15 ruling did not enter it, because it was then uncertainty in an estimate that did not yet exist. That has changed. The W-908 re-estimate is on disk (company/engineering/notes/2026-10-15-first-light-reestimate.md) and puts the dates at about 25% at full scope, which the founder restored the same day. The slip rule moves go/no-go day for day if EDD-008 misses 10-28 (F-01 met 10-23 on 10-15). A measured 75% chance of a miss is an event, not just an estimate, so it is entered. Impact is 3 and not the proposed 4. A date slip delays one release, and the company keeps shipping (the impact-4 line is 'can't ship for a day or a gate is bypassed'). The impact-5 way this fails under date pressure (a thin or skipped privacy or readiness review) is already R-020 and is not counted twice. Re-score on W-1121, the full-scope re-estimate with odds and a cut order.

mitigation.summary: Full-scope re-estimate with odds and a cut order (W-1121), the dates and cut-order proposal to the founder (W-1122), the slip rule, and the pre-declared cuts (challenges at 11-06, the swap only with F-26 by 10-30).
mitigation.paperOnly: W-1121 and W-1122 are backlog. The cut order is not decided, and no tool checks the slip rule.

risks.title: A social surface reaches learners without a named human moderator
risks.description: Proposed as FL-08 (status.json, L4 I3, 'social has no named human moderator'), re-framed. The 4x3 reading is scope loss: with no moderator, privacy gate P4.3 fails and the prediction swap is absent from release 1. That is a founder decision with a due date and an if-it-slips line (F-26, 10-30; founder record 2026-10-15, objection 2). It stays in status.json and the founder inbox, not here. What the register carries is the harm side: a swap or any social path (one learner shown a friend's sealed prediction, a friend link between a stranger and a 13 to 15 year old) is built and reaches learners with nobody to act on a report within 24 hours (1 hour for a child in danger). Likelihood is 2. P4.3 and the founder record both keep it out of the build, but both are paper, and nothing in the build or the deploy gate refuses a social route. Impact is 5 (learners harmed). Share links S1 to S5 carry no learner content and are not in scope here.

mitigation.summary: F-26 (a human moderator and a cover, due 10-30). P4.3 ruled by 11-09. PRD-003 starts no work before F-26 beyond an EDD draft (W-1131). The swap's tier-2 readiness record must show the report path and its owner before approval.
mitigation.paperOnly: F-26 is open. P4.3 is a gate document. No check in the build, the readiness tool or the deploy refuses a social route without a moderator.

risks.title: The accounts kill switch is a founder-approved redeploy, not instant
risks.description: Proposed as FL-09 (status.json, L3 I3). SPIKE-002 R3 (accounts branch, 2f5c500): the code reads ACCOUNTS_ENABLED per request, but Vercel applies a changed variable only to new deployments. So 'off' means setting the variable and then a redeploy, and every deploy needs the founder's approval (CLAUDE.md). Time to off is therefore founder availability (R-013) plus a build, not seconds. Likelihood is 2 today. Previews run on the test database with staff addresses only and behind Deployment Protection, and production has no accounts variables, so an accounts fault now harms nobody. It goes to 3 at go-live (W-1142). Impact is 4, not the proposed 3. When it matters, a fault in a learner-data route (for example a log or response leaking an email; readiness gap A-6) stays live for the whole approval-plus-build window, which keeps a gate (P1) bypassed longer. Readiness record: company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-accounts.md, gap A-3.

mitigation.summary: The runbook states 'set the variable, redeploy' with a measured time to off (W-1150). platform-engineer proposes a control that needs no deploy: a Vercel Firewall rule denying /api/account/*, or Instant Rollback to a pre-on deployment, or Edge Config (which needs a decision record). The founder decides whether a kill-switch action is pre-approved. The accounts readiness approval requires A-3.
mitigation.paperOnly: No runbook line, no measured time to off, no control that works without a deploy, and no founder pre-approval.

The app uses no next/image, "use cache" or "use server" (review), so likelihood is 2, not 4; nobody has shown the advisories unreachable, so it is not 1. risks.title: A framed lesson fails silently in production: no meter for never-ready or refused progress
risks.description: Readiness record 2026-10-26-lesson-frames-pilot.md R-new-1 (feat/lesson-frames-pilot). With NEXT_PUBLIC_LESSON_FRAMES=pilot-50, DemoFrame logs a refused bridge message and a frame that never sends ready only outside production. A learner sees a blank card or finishes a framed lesson whose completion is not recorded, and nobody learns of it. Likelihood 3 once the flag is on (a second origin, a new bridge, 42 of 50 pilot lessons changed in a week); 1 while the flag is off, which is the only state approved. Impact 3: lost completions and blank cards for up to 50 lessons, silent.

mitigation.summary: A production frame-error meter before production flag-on (W-2111); C6/C7 runs and the frame QA copy before it (W-2100, W-2096). Flag-on production is not approved in the readiness record until W-2111 is done.

risks.title: The lesson-frames staleness gate blocks deploys
risks.description: Readiness record R-new-2 and objection O1: as first built, tests/lesson-frames failed npm run verify whenever a pilot lesson or the kit sources changed, and 42 of 50 pilot lessons and globals.css (18 commits in 15 days) change often (code review R14). O1 was ruled (company/decisions/2026-10-26-lesson-frames-gate-scope.md) and coded at 3ef3619ca: freshness rules block only flag-on builds, in next.config.mjs. Residual: every flag-on build is refused after any globals.css or pilot-lesson change until prune or rebuild (W-2106, W-2110). Likelihood 4 at flag-on, impact 2 (a delayed deploy, no learner harm).

mitigation.summary: O1 scoping at 3ef3619ca (flag-off deploys unaffected); kit sourceHash decoupled from all of globals.css (W-2106); a runbook step for flag-on: prune or rebuild, then commit (W-2110); prune handles stale-kit (W-2105).
